result.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` in SalesforceCalendarService that runs on every instantiation, before any check of whether the existing access token is still valid, and with no timeout/abort signal. A slow/hanging token endpoint would block all Salesforce calendar operations even when the stored token is usable, and the extra round-trip fires on every service construction. This is a real, verifiable behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, a new fetch call is added at line 63-75 that refreshes OAuth tokens unconditionally during connection initialization. This fetch has no timeout or AbortController, meaning if the Salesforce token endpoint is slow or unresponsive, the entire connection construction will hang indefinitely. Unlike other integrations in this diff that use refreshOAuthTokens wrapper with conditional logic (checking APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED), Salesforce makes this call unconditionally on every connection. This is a real defect - a stalled network request would block operations even when existing credentials might still be valid.
